label: no
controls_available: Difficulty 4 uses 14 heptagonal faces, a six-twist scramble, and an eight-twist budget.
Full interaction permits Mobius panning by dragging the Poincare disc.
A short left-button canvas click on a centered face applies a counter-clockwise twist; a short right-button click applies a clockwise twist.
RESET SCRAMBLE and CERTIFY are visible; FRESH CHALLENGE is available after failure. These are reset or administrative controls, not an autonomous outcome control.
autonomous_processes: None after initial render: with no new agent input, the sticker state and Mobius view remain unchanged.
Hover movement can redraw a face highlight, but it is agent-driven and does not change outcome state.
The shared clock can advance registered timers or animation frames, but this mechanic registers no task timer, animation loop, physics update, or other autonomous state transition.
grouped_control_modes: D_twist: every full-mode canvas-click twist occurrence across seeds, rounds, and attempts, with left/counter-clockwise and right/clockwise directions as the action parameter.
D_pan: full-mode Mobius drag occurrences; these change only the view and are not outcome-affecting.
Reset, certification, and fresh-challenge controls are administrative/reset operations rather than outcome-affecting grouped modes.

clause_i.reason: For D_twist, the generated scramble and inverse face/direction sequence vary by seed, while the first twist has the same empty I_t across seeds. No observation-free q can choose a guaranteed delayed-optimal face and direction for every such history.

clause_ii.reason: A zero-length bounded window contains the current screenshot, which visibly contains the colored sticker arrangement and face geometry. Because the puzzle is static between inputs and has no future autonomous randomness, a screenshot-based policy can choose the next face and direction from that frame and its prior actions.

clause_iii.reason: With no new action, Circle Limit Twist has no non-clock task-state evolution: the current sticker state, view, twist budget, and activation geometry stay fixed. Any legal twist remains available with the same effect after a positive wait, so Q(H_t^tau,a) equals Q(H_t,a) and the action advantage does not strictly decrease. A possible overall play-time deadline is excluded by the definition as clock-only loss. No choice of D, positive Delta, or bounded window can supply the missing autonomous process.

common_visible_process: None. The rendered scramble is static; only pointer event handlers mutate the view or sticker state, and the same absence of autonomous evolution defeats clause (iii).

pre_run.reason: There is no autonomous outcome phase: solving requires the agent's outcome-affecting twist actions, followed by administrative certification. A pre-run rate is therefore not defined, and the mathematical classification is already No because clause (iii) fails.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 4 is face_count 14, scramble_length 6, move_budget 8; full mode is Mobius drag plus left/right click; the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame.

The generator reads the selected control difficulty, creates a fixed initial sticker state from a seed-specific scramble, records a finite move budget, and exports no autonomous time-dependent puzzle variable.
applyTwist changes the sticker state only when called by an input handler, subject to the activation aperture and twist budget.
Full-mode pointer events update the view during a drag and invoke a twist on pointerup for a short click; there is no autonomous task-state update between input events.
render initializes the scramble, view, counters, and event listeners, then draws the canvas; reset and certification are explicit user controls.
The mechanic stylesheet defines static layout, cursor, and visual-state rules but no Circle Limit Twist animation or timed movement.

The grader accepts full-mode canvas-click twists and replays only pan/twist events, sticker permutations, aperture checks, and the move budget; the outcome has no elapsed-time or motion-state condition.
The verifier independently replays the same static event transcript and solved-state condition, with no autonomous-time criterion.
The scripted solver applies the seed-provided inverse scramble through visible full-mode drags and canvas clicks, confirming that progress is action-driven rather than a timed phase.
The frozen definition requires a common visibly evidenced autonomous process that makes a useful action strictly worse during Delta; clock-only deadline loss is excluded.
